title: Individual and collective epistemic virtue in science
core_idea: Investigate the explanatory role of epistemic virtue in accounting for the success of science as a social institution; examine structural explanations that attribute collective success to economic and incentive structures (virtue radicalism), analyze the credibility crisis in the social and behavioral sciences as a challenge to those accounts, and aim to argue for the importance of individual epistemic virtue for establishing, maintaining, and reforming social structures that support reliable knowledge production.
tldr: Assesses whether individual epistemic virtues are needed for the collective success of science by critiquing structural explanations (virtue radicalism) and using the credibility crisis as a test case, with the goal of defending the role of virtuous scientists in sustaining scientific institutions.
